subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Endometriosis and adenomyosis: chocolate cysts, DIE and stepped care

steps.tx: **Endometriosis** means endometrial glands and stroma growing outside the uterus, and it commonly causes painful periods, deep pain during intercourse, chronic pelvic pain and infertility. **Chocolate cysts** are ovarian endometriomas filled with old blood that look ground glass on ultrasound. **Deep infiltrating disease** forms tender uterosacral nodules and obliterates the pouch of Douglas. Adenomyosis instead enlarges the uterus, which feels boggy and tender, with heavy painful periods.
steps.say: Endometriosis occurs when endometrial tissue grows outside the uterus and causes painful periods, painful intercourse and infertility. Ovarian chocolate cysts contain old blood and are seen as a ground glass pattern on ultrasound. Deep disease produces tender nodules along the uterosacral ligaments and closes the pouch of Douglas. Adenomyosis grows within the uterine wall, so the uterus feels boggy and tender and bleeds heavily with pain.

steps.tx: **Medical therapy** starts with NSAIDs for pain and combined hormonal pills that suppress endometrial tissue growth. **Progestins** such as dienogest control pain and shrink lesions, while **GnRH analogues** induce a low estrogen state and always need add back therapy to protect bone. Elagolix is an oral antagonist option that can cause hot flushes. Mild asymptomatic disease may be observed, and assisted reproduction is chosen by severity, with laparoscopy, IUI or IVF.
steps.say: Medical treatment begins with NSAIDs for pain relief and combined hormonal pills that suppress endometrial growth. Progestins such as dienogest are used to relieve pain and shrink lesions. GnRH analogues lower estrogen strongly, so add back therapy protects bone during treatment. Elagolix offers an oral antagonist option but commonly causes hot flushes. Doctors observe mild disease without symptoms and select laparoscopy, IUI or IVF according to severity.

steps.tx: **Cystectomy** strips the ovarian cyst wall and relieves pain, but it can lower ovarian reserve measured by AMH. **Ablation** fulgurates surface lesions, while **deep excision** removes bowel or bladder disease with a multidisciplinary team. For adenomyosis, the **levonorgestrel IUS** comes first and often controls bleeding well. Focal adenomyomectomy preserves fertility in selected cases, and hysterectomy gives definitive treatment when childbearing is complete.

steps.tx: This **laparoscopic view** shows an opened **chocolate cyst** releasing dark old blood, exactly as endometriosis appears during surgery. Nearby, dark **uterosacral nodules** mark deep infiltrating disease that needs careful mapping before excision. Stripping the cyst wall can lower AMH, so surgeons balance complete removal against ovarian reserve. Deep nodules near bowel or ureter require a multidisciplinary team for safe excision.

steps.tx: **Malignant transformation** is rare, but long standing ovarian endometriosis can rarely develop clear cell or endometrioid cancer, so new concerning features need imaging. **Adolescents** with severe early dysmenorrhea and school absence need evaluation for obstructive Mullerian anomalies. **Menopause care** avoids unopposed estrogen because it can regrow lesions, and chronic pain benefits from neuromodulators, physiotherapy and psychological support.

Adolescents with severe early pain and school absence need evaluation for obstructive anomalies. Menopause care avoids unopposed estrogen because it can regrow lesions. Chronic pelvic pain improves with neuromodulators, physiotherapy and psychological support.
